title: Snakeguard: modeled ₹992/qtl left, Kayamkulam → Anchal
summary: January 2024: reported snakeguard prices at Kayamkulam and Anchal imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 100% of 29 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹992 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 260 same-variety market pairs screened for snakeguard in January 2024; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Anchal report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2024
scenes.caption: Kayamkulam (Kerala) and Anchal (Kerala) both reported snakeguard prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 29 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kayamkulam reported a median ₹3,400 per quintal. Anchal reported a median ₹4,600 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,300/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,300 per quintal, and Anchal was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 65 km by road
scenes.caption: 65 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~1 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹14/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹883 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹653 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Anchal report, the rule selects 29 of 29 modeled shipping days. 29 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹992 per quintal (₹748 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Snakeguard route from Kayamkulam to Anchal was positive on 100% of matched days in January 2024. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹99,200, or ₹74,800 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to snakeguard
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹14/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Snakeguard route from Kayamkulam to Anchal was positive on 100% of matched days in January 2024. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹99,200, or ₹74,800 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
